items.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
items.summary: By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that's already within its ecosystem
items.content:
Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.

By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.

Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.

As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.

Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.

Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.

The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.

items.title: OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits
items.summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has released internal perplexity scores for the entire GPT series for the first time, up to an unreleased model beyond the current generation. The metric shows that core capabilities emerge at surprisingly precise thresholds. Pachocki is push
items.content:
OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits

OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes making perplexity an industry standard for AI progress and releases internal data on the GPT series through GPT-6.

The data shows capabilities emerging at fixed thresholds, from fluent conversation in GPT-3.5 and logical reasoning in GPT-4 to solving complex math problems.

Pachocki calls for leading labs to agree on shared limits until better oversight methods exist, since newer models could bypass existing safety checks.

OpenAI ties capabilities like fluent conversation and math breakthroughs to specific scores. For the first time, chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is showing where the GPT series sits on that scale, up to an unreleased model beyond GPT-6.

Pachocki wants to make perplexity a common measure of progress for the AI industry and published internal scores for the GPT series in a bl o g post . The metric has long been standard in AI research and Transformer development because it reliably measures how well a pretrained base model predicts the next token in a text.

Lower scores mean more accurate predictions. A perplexity of 2 roughly means the model is as uncertain about the next token as if it were choosing between two equally likely options.

Before it stopped publishing openly, OpenAI often released perplexity scores to show how its models were improving. Releasing them again is a trade-off, Pachocki writes . While rivals get a clearer picture of where OpenAI stands, he says, the need for shared safety standards outweighs that downside. He hopes for a common scientific foundation that lets labs coordinate their pace of development at critical points.

Capabilities emerge at distinct perplexity thresholds

Pachocki says many capabilities of modern models map surprisingly closely to specific perplexity scores, even though it wasn't clear beforehand that they would appear at those thresholds. He reports the figures on a logarithmic scale called log-perplexity, where lower scores are still better. In his account, GPT-3.5 first enabled fluent conversation at around 0.99, laying the groundwork for the original ChatGPT. At about 0.91, GPT-4 unlocked productive chain-of-thought reasoning, or working through problems step by step. Below 0.8, he writes, transformative capabilities emerged in cybersecurity and math .

The lower a base model's log-perplexity, the more capabilities it shows, according to OpenAI. Starting in 2026, the scores drop much more steeply than in earlier years. | Image: OpenAI The published chart plots OpenAI's base-model log-perplexity by release or evaluation date through November 2026. It covers GPT-5 , GPT-5.1 , GPT-5.2 , GPT-5.3-Codex , GPT-5.4 , GPT-5.5 , GPT-5.6 Sol , GPT-6 Astra , and GPT-6.2 Astra , plus an internal model at around 0.73.

OpenAI's models deliver math breakthroughs in a Slack thread

OpenAI has been feeding its models open math problems for more than a year. Starting with a model at about 0.76 log-perplexity, the models began producing breakthrough results, Pachocki writes. For researchers with a math background, he says, it was "deeply surreal" to watch solutions to longstanding questions pop up one after another in a single Slack thread.

Those results include a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem , one of the Millennium Prize problems, though it hasn't been fully verified yet. The same goes for the proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis found by Claude and an Anthropic researcher. Pachocki thinks deep learning research itself could see something similar as soon as 2027, bringing a sudden avalanche of core advances in AI training.

A footnote says the sharp acceleration in the chart starting in 2026 comes mostly from long-term research and compute investments and less from automation. Even so, AI itself has contributed major design work on OpenAI's latest models, according to the post.

items.content:
Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data

LaLiga, Spain's top men's professional football league, disclosed a data breach that exposed personal information belonging to users of its services and those of some affiliated clubs.

According to the organization, the incident occurred between November 14 and 16, and the attacker extracted data from compromised systems.

LaLiga organizes Spain’s top two men’s professional football divisions.

The top league is one of the world’s most prominent football leagues, where clubs with a global audience, such as Real Madrid, FC Barcelona, and Atlético Madrid, play.

On November 16, the organization’s security team identified the source of the unauthorized access and implemented measures to block the attack and stop the data extraction.

“LALIGA was the target of a cyberattack on one of its technology platforms for fan services,” reads the announcement .

“Between November 14 and 16, a cybercriminal gained unauthorized access to the platform and extracted personal data belonging to users registered for digital services offered by LALIGA and some clubs.”

LaLiga underlined that the incident was confined to a specific platform and did not extend to other systems that support the running of the competitions.

After implementing containment measures, LaLiga launched an investigation to determine the scope of the incident and introduced more thorough monitoring to detect future attempts to breach its systems.

The football organizer also reported the incident to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) and filed a complaint with the National Police’s Central Cybercrime Unit.

Impacted clubs were also directly notified, and actions to inform impacted fans are being coordinated.

At the time of writing, no ransomware group has claimed responsibility for the attack on LaLiga.

BleepingComputer has contacted the organization to learn more about the attack and which clubs were impacted, but we have not received a response as of publication.

items.title: Signal blocks screenshots by Apple, Google operating systems to protect data from AI agents
items.summary: Google’s Gemini Intelligence and Apple's Siri AI "are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy," Signal said.
items.content:
Image: Brett Jordan via Unsplash Signal blocks screenshots by Apple, Google operating systems to protect data from AI agents

The encrypted messaging platform Signal has announced it will by default stop users from taking screenshots of messages if they are using Google or Apple operating systems, a move fueled by concerns about how the tech giants deploy artificial intelligence agents.

Last year, the widely used messaging app restricted Microsoft 11 users from screenshotting and keeping messages. Similar restrictions will now apply to Google’s Gemini Intelligence and Apple's Siri AI, Signal Foundation president Meredith Whittaker said in a Friday blog post.

“These agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy,” the blog post said. “This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission.”

Whittaker said Signal plans to specifically restrict the agentic systems integrated into iOS 27 and versions of Android where Signal detects AI assistants trying to read text.

The operating systems’ AI agents attempt to glean information from users by scanning what’s on their screens, Whittaker said, and in doing so hoover up the data in order to “answer your questions and do your bidding,” the blog post said.

Whittaker warned the agents are making the captured data accessible to random local databases and remote servers at random.

“All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation,” the blog post said.

While screenshots won’t be permitted by default, the blog post said users who choose to can disable the block in settings.

The “remedy is incomplete,” Whittaker warned, because blocking screenshots does not address “other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data, such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.”

The dearth of effective tools available to Signal and other app developers to use to stop AI agents from weakening privacy is a significant concern, the blog post said.

Whittaker condemned Microsoft, Apple and Google for failing to provide app developers with a mechanism to block agents’ access to data without significantly compromising the “core user experience.”

The same lack of cooperation from tech giants is also to blame for Signal’s inability to place the restrictions on macOS, the blog post said. Additionally, Signal has struggled with a profound lack of documentation about how the agents function.

“Without better documentation and clear technical specifications, it will be increasingly difficult for Signal to provide robust privacy and security to the many millions of people who rely on us,” Whittaker said.

“These three operating systems are the oceans in which Signal, and other applications, must swim; they dictate the conditions of life for the application ecosystem,” the blog post said of Apple, Google and Microsoft. “These agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy.”

Whittaker called on the companies to provide an easy way for users to opt-out of data access permissions tools, stop third-party agents from accessing data without users’ consent and bolster documentation lending transparency to how agents work.

Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Microsoft and Google declined to comment.

items.content:
FBI reportedly facing second data breach involving National Crime Information Center

The FBI is reportedly investigating a data breach involving the National Crime Information Center, a database used by U.S. law enforcement agencies that contains information on criminals, fugitives and missing people.

The FBI did not respond to requests for comment but sources told CNN and later the Associated Press that the cyberattack took place on Thursday.

The database, known as the NCIC, is used among local, state and federal agencies to share information on criminals and investigations. It offers law enforcement agencies data on outstanding warrants and contains sensitive information of value to criminals and others.

President Donald Trump told Fox News this weekend that he had been briefed on the incident, adding: “I will say that it’s not good — I don’t like that.” He went on to say the breach may allow the public to have access to investigative files related to him.

If confirmed, this would be the second cybersecurity incident affecting the FBI this year. In September, the ShinyHunters hacking group breached the FBI’s job site and allegedly stole troves of information on every FBI employee.

Multiple people were arrested as part of the investigation into the ShinyHunters breach, including a cybersecurity expert from Canada .

The U.S. government has suffered from several cybersecurity incidents this year in addition to the attacks on the FBI.

Last month, hackers took down a platform used by all federal bankruptcy courts across the country and a ransomware attack in August targeted the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). The ATF called the breach a “major incident” and said it involved a computer system containing information about targets of investigations.

The departments of Defense and Transportation also experienced cybersecurity incidents this year, and the Department of Agriculture was forced to take offline multiple systems used to facilitate payments between the agency and farmers after a cyberattack last week .

items.title: New York judge declines to block Kalshi from operating in the state for now
items.content:
Kalshi can keep operating under a temporary court reprieve in which a judge put off New York’s attempt to halt the prediction market platform’s operations in the state, at least for now.

In a hearing Monday, Judge Melissa Crane of the New York State Supreme Court said she preferred to let both the New York Attorney General's office and Kalshi's attorneys flesh out their respective arguments rather than grant an immediate estraining order. New York sought to block Kalshi from offering any sports-related prediction markets in New York, raising concerns that — because the company is headquartered in the state — Kalshi might be blocked from offering its products anywhere in the U.S. if the motion were granted. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, Kalshi's federal regulator, even warned of the possibility last week in an unsuccessful, last-ditch effort to get a federal judge to intervene.

The judge expressed concerns about how any ruling might be appealed, according to attorney Daniel Wallach , while noting the current status quo is Kalshi continuing to operate as it has been for the past year. While Kalshi won its reprieve on Monday, the broader dispute will continue, and may have major consequences for the popular platform's future as courts throughout the country continue to debate whether prediction markets are derivatives or gambling products.

Judge Crane heard arguments from lawyers with Attorney General Letitia James' office and Kalshi over whether the firm had the right to offer sports and other prediction markets in New York, where it’s headquartered. Kalshi has contended that its licensing as a federally regulated designated contract market allows it to offer event contracts (the technical term for what trades on such prediction markets platforms) nationally, while New York — alongside numerous other states — has argued that these products violate state gambling regulations.

The judge was concerned about the scope of the potential restraining order, noting that federal courts are also involved, leading to her preference for a sped-up briefing schedule to hash out whether or not the court would order any halt to trading at Kalshi. That schedule has not yet been set.

In the interim, the judge asked the parties to sort out "safeguards" for people between the ages of 18 and 21 who can access Kalshi, given New York bars gambling to under-21-year-olds. She scheduled a tentative hearing for next Monday if this remains an outstanding issue.

The case is one of many that states around the U.S. have brought against prediction market providers in mostly state courts. Kalshi and other providers have fought back, including by trying to file preemptive strikes in federal courts, with mixed results.

CFTC Chair Mike Selig has stated numerous times that prediction markets fall under his agency's exclusive jurisdiction, and that states were intruding by trying to enforce their gambling regulations.

The U.S. Supreme Court is likely to take up the issue, after three appellate courts ruled in favor of states and a fourth ruled in favor of Kalshi this year. Kalshi has until Dec. 7, 2026 to file a response to the state of New Jersey in arguing over whether the court should take up the case at all. The Supreme Court is expected to announce whether it will hear arguments early next year.

items.title: Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access
items.summary: The China-aligned threat actor known as Webworm is suspected to be using a custom version of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge tool in an attempt to remove recognizable detection fingerprints, while disguising it as network-monitoring software to establish covert remote access
items.content:
The China-aligned threat actor known as Webworm is suspected to be using a custom version of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge tool in an attempt to remove recognizable detection fingerprints, while disguising it as network-monitoring software to establish covert remote access to compromised networks.

The modified variant "implements various tricks to hide itself from security tools," Rapid7 said in an analysis, attributing it to the adversarial collective with moderate confidence.

First publicly detailed by Broadcom-owned Symantec in September 2022, Webworm is the name assigned to a China-aligned nation-state group that has targeted government entities, IT services, and electric power companies across Russia, Georgia, Mongolia, and several other Asian nations.

One of the tools used by the threat actor is a legitimate software called SoftEther VPN , with the bridge acting as a pathway connecting the compromised network and the attacker-controlled infrastructure.

The latest findings from Rapid7 revolve around a Windows executable (" netcapa.exe "), which is a modified build of SoftEther VPN Bridge ("vpnbridge_x64.exe") version 4.44, build 9807. The modified version, rebranded as NtMonitor VPN, masquerades itself as Network Monitor Software from a company called Network Systems Solutions Inc. The artifact was uploaded to VirusTotal around mid-January 2026.

"The PDB path included in the executable reads C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\SoftEtherVPN_Stable\SoftEtherVPN_Stable\SoftEtherVPN_Stable\src\DebugFiles\pdb\x64_Release\vpnbridge.pdb," the cybersecurity company said. "As such, the tool doesn't hide its identity from reverse engineers, only external interactions."

The renaming is also said to be inconsistent, with many registry key paths still referencing the program as "SoftEther Project," even though a number of other occurrences of "SoftEther VPN" have been replaced by "NtMonitor VPN."

One of the most noticeable changes identified in the altered version is the use of innocuous-looking HTTP endpoints "/update/alive.cgi" and "/update/picture.cgi" to replace "/vpnsvc/vpn.cgi" and "/vpnsvc/connect.cgi," respectively, so that they look like ordinary web application activity.

It also changes the protocol watermark used by SoftEther VPN as part of the handshake process when initiating communication to help the tool distinguish protocol traffic from ordinary HTTP requests. When the connecting client is found to speak the expected protocol, it proceeds with the handshake. If the check fails, the server returns a decoy HTTP response.

The modified version swaps the GIF-based watermark used by the stock SoftEther VPN utility for a PNG-based watermark so as to bypass existing detection signatures based on the GIF watermark.

Some of the other changes introduced to the program are listed below -

What's interesting here is that the attackers have not been found to introduce any new functionality to the tool, indicating the primary focus was on stealth.

"It seems like they methodically analyzed SoftEther's detection surface and implemented counter-measures to all of the easy ways a detection engineer may target it," Rapid7 said, calling the latest evolution a hybrid approach that brings together the attacker's use of custom malware and dual-use tools.

"We are observing a sort of hybrid of the two — stock SoftEther software that is not trojanized, but rebuilt from source in a way that erases much of its detection fingerprint."

당시 해커는 한전의 주요 서비스와 관련된 대규모 데이터를 탈취했다고 주장했으며, 개인정보를 포함한 자료의 외부 유출 가능성이 제기됐다.

데일리시큐는 해당 게시물과 해커의 주장을 확인하고 한전의 개인정보 유출 가능성을 보도했다. 당시에는 실제 침해 여부와 데이터의 진위에 대한 한전 측의 공식 확인이 필요한 상황이었다.

그러나 23일 개인정보위 발표를 통해 한전ON과 SRM 이용자 정보가 실제 유출된 사실이 공식 확인됐다. 데일리시큐가 단독으로 제기했던 한전의 대규모 개인정보 유출 의혹이 근거 없는 해커의 주장이 아니라 실제 발생한 침해사고였다는 사실이 확인된 것이다.

개인정보위에 따르면 한전은 19일 해커로부터 정보 탈취 사실을 알리는 이메일을 받았고, 다크웹 게시 사실을 확인했다. 20일에는 해커로부터 확보한 샘플 데이터도 확인했다.

한전은 이러한 사실을 토대로 22일 오후 6시경 개인정보위에 개인정보 유출을 신고했다.

■ 한전ON 65만 명·전자조달시스템 87만 명…주민등록번호와 금융정보까지 유출

개인정보위가 발표한 유출 규모는 한전ON 고객 약 65만 명과 전자조달시스템(SRM) 이용자 약 87만 명 등 합산 약 152만 명분이다.

한전ON에서는 성명, 주민등록번호 및 외국인등록번호, 전화번호, 고객번호, 계좌 또는 카드정보 등이 유출됐다.

전자조달시스템에서는 성명, 주민등록번호 및 외국인등록번호, 소속, 사번, 이메일 등이 유출된 것으로 확인됐다.

단순한 연락처 유출에 그치지 않고 주민등록번호와 금융 관련 정보까지 포함돼 있어 피해자들의 2차 피해 가능성에 대한 우려가 크다.

특히 한전ON은 일반 전력 이용 고객이 사용하는 서비스인 반면, SRM은 한전의 입찰·계약·조달 업무와 관련된 시스템이다. 서로 성격이 다른 두 시스템에서 대규모 개인정보 유출이 확인됐다는 점에서 공격 경로와 시스템 간 연관성에 대한 조사가 필요하다.

현재 발표된 152만 명은 두 시스템의 피해 규모를 합산한 수치다. 중복 이용자를 제외한 실제 피해 인원이 정확히 몇 명인지는 추가 확인이 필요하다.

개인정보위는 23일 초동대응반을 구성해 한전에 대한 현장점검에 착수했다.

조사에서는 해커의 최초 침입 경로와 개인정보 반출 과정, 실제 피해 규모를 확인하는 한편 한전이 개인정보 보호법에 따른 안전조치 의무를 제대로 이행했는지 살펴볼 예정이다.

개인정보 유출을 인지한 이후 이용자 통지와 관계기관 신고가 적절하게 이뤄졌는지도 조사 대상이다. 법 위반사항이 확인되면 관련 법령에 따라 처분할 방침이다.

개인정보위는 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA)과 함께 유출된 정보가 온라인에서 불법 유통되지 않도록 모니터링을 강화하고 있다.

개인정보위는 한전으로부터 유출 통지를 받은 이용자들에게 출처가 불분명한 인터넷 주소(URL) 클릭이나 앱 설치, 개인정보 인증 요구 등에 각별히 주의할 것을 당부했다.

정부는 공공기관의 개인정보 보호 책임을 강화하기 위해 중대·반복 위반 시 과징금을 최대 50억 원까지 상향하는 방안과 기관장 징계 책임 강화 등을 추진하고 있다. 이번 사고에 대한 구체적인 책임과 제재 수준은 향후 조사 결과에 따라 결정될 전망이다.

주민등록번호와 금융정보가 포함된 대규모 개인정보가 외부로 유출된 만큼, 단순한 사고 경위 확인을 넘어 유출정보의 추가 확산 차단과 피해자 보호, 공공기관의 개인정보 관리 책임에 대한 철저한 조사가 요구된다.

items.title: CrowdStrike to purchase Zscaler for $43.9 billion
items.summary: “We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen,” CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said.
items.content:
Image: Zscaler via Facebook CrowdStrike to purchase Zscaler for $43.9 billion

Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike will acquire cloud security company Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal announced on Monday morning.

The deal will see two of the largest cybersecurity companies consolidate, merging Zscaler’s tools with CrowdStrike’s suite of cyberattack response services, endpoint security platforms, and threat intelligence offerings. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue to run Zscaler and will join CrowdStrike’s board of directors.

CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said the acquisition of Zscaler will allow them to build “cybersecurity’s operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely.”

“We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen,” he said.

News of a potential acquisition emerged on Friday when Bloomberg reported that CrowdStrike was circling Zscaler, which had a market value of about $32 billion as of Friday.

Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 shares of CrowdStrike common stock for each share of Zscaler common stock, or $260.41 per Zscaler share. Existing CrowdStrike shareholders are expected to own approximately 84.1% of Zscaler once the deal closes.

CrowdStrike said the acquisition would allow it to sell its platforms to Zscaler’s 8,000 customers, including 50 percent of the Fortune 500. The company explained that while CrowdStrike’s tools focus on securing endpoints and data, Zscaler’s products are adept at “securing the connections between them.”

“With Zscaler, CrowdStrike will enter network security, cybersecurity’s largest single addressable market segment,” a company spokesperson explained.

Chaudhry warned that AI agents are “rapidly becoming the new weakest link” and said the deal with CrowdStrike will accelerate their ability to expand their zero trust tools to a larger customer base.

“We see a significant opportunity to offer customers far superior protection in a rapidly evolving threat landscape and enable enterprises to safely adopt AI,” he said.

Zscaler’s products will be sold through CrowdStrike’s system of resellers and distributors.

Both companies released their quarterly earnings reports on Monday, with Zscaler reporting $949.3 million in revenue for the first quarter — a 20% increase compared to last year’s first quarter.

The $43.9 billion figure tops last year’s largest deal, when Google purchased cloud security company Wiz for $32 billion.

GlobeTopper loses $2.5 million after hackers steal $70k in gift cards

A cyberattack disrupted operations at B2B top-up solutions provider GlobeTopper, causing an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue, while the attacker redeemed digital gift cards worth $70,000.

Parent company iQSTEL said that the intrusion was detected on October 22 and GlobeTopper responded by suspending its platform and starting an investigation.

GlobeTopper is a business-to-business digital gift card distributor. Various retailers, fintech apps, and rewards platforms use its API. According to the platform’s website , it is used by more than 4,000 brands across 65 countries, including IKEA, Adidas, Spotify, Target, and Roblox.

In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), iQSTEL said that GlobeTopper detected more unauthorized activity the day after it identified the attack. In response, the company "took the platform and all affected servers offline" in the early hours of October 23 to investigate and fix the problem.

The company deployed a completely rebuilt platform on AWS on October 31, while commercial operations were restored in stages, starting November 1.

GlobeTopper says the attacker obtained certain client API credentials and integration keys, which have been revoked and replaced, and it has observed no unauthorized use of them yet.

“During its investigation, the Company determined that the unauthorized party obtained API credentials and integration keys of certain GlobeTopper business customers,” iQSTEL says .

“All affected credentials and integration keys have been revoked and rotated, and affected business customers have been issued new credentials subject to additional access restrictions.”

The company further stated that an investigation is ongoing to determine whether other customer, personal, payment, or provider data was accessed or acquired.

Regarding the digital gift cards the attackers redeemed, the company says it cannot block, recover, or reclaim them, and will incur the losses.

iQSTEL said the incident hurt GlobeTopper’s fourth-quarter transaction volume and operating results, but as of the filing, it has not determined it to be material.

BleepingComputer has emailed iQSTEL with additional questions regarding the incident, but the company declined to share further information.

At the time of writing, no ransomware groups have listed iQSTEL or GlobeTopper as victims on their extortion portals.

items.content:
보안제품을 도입해도 제품끼리 연결되지 않고, 현장에서 겪은 시행착오는 다른 기업에 충분히 공유되지 않는다. 한국트러스트연합이 출범하며 주목한 국내 보안 현장의 문제다. 보안 수요기관이 해결할 과제를 제시하면 공급기업이 해법을 마련하고, 학계와 전문가가 효과를 검증하는 협력체계를 만들겠다는 구상이다.

한국트러스트연합(KOTA·Korea Trust Alliance. 회장 김승현)이 11월 23일 서울 한국프레스센터 20층 프레스클럽에서 창립총회를 열고 공식 출범했다. 총회에서는 정관 제정안과 임원 선임안을 만장일치로 의결하고 김승현 법무법인 율촌 고문을 초대 회장으로 선출했다.

KOTA의 설립 목적은 ‘현장에서 작동하는 보안’이라고 볼 수 있다. 개별 기술의 우수성을 설명하는 데서 나아가 여러 제품과 운영체계를 실제로 연결하고, 그 결과를 수요자와 공급자가 공동의 지식으로 축적하겠다는 것이다.

KOTA 설립에는 금융·통신 등 주요 산업의 보안 수요자와 보안기업, 학계·법률·공공 분야 전문가 등 발기인 61명이 참여했다. 수요자와 보안 분야 참여자가 각각 20명으로 전체의 32.8%씩을 차지했다. 학계 9명, 법무법인 6명, 공공 3명과 언론·AI·IT 분야 각 1명도 합류했다.

수요자와 공급자의 참여 비중을 맞춘 구성은 기술을 사용하는 기관이 현장의 어려움을 구체적으로 제시하고, 공급기업과 전문가가 함께 해결책을 검토하도록 하겠다는 취지다.

금융회사에서 IT시스템 개발·운영과 정보보안 업무를 수행하고 정보보호최고책임자(CISO)를 역임한 김승현 회장은 취임 인사에서 기술 도입 이후의 책임과 협력을 강조했다.

김 회장은 “기술을 얼마나 빠르게 도입하느냐를 넘어 그 기술을 얼마나 안전하고 책임 있게 활용할 수 있느냐가 중요해지고 있다”고 말했다. 신뢰를 구축하려면 기술과 제도에 더해 책임, 투명성, 전문성, 지속적인 실천이 필요하다고 강조했다.

질의응답에서는 기존 제로트러스트 보안협회와의 차별성에 대한 질문이 나왔다. 김 회장은 기존 보안시장이 공급자 관점에서 발전해 온 과정에서 수요자의 요구를 충분히 함께 검토할 기회가 부족했다고 설명했다. KOTA는 수요자가 필요로 하는 보안체계를 구체화하고, 적용 사례와 시행착오를 공유하는 데 무게를 두겠다는 것이다.

설립 경과보고에 따르면 준비 논의는 지난 6월 시작됐다. 전문가 면담과 참여 의향 수렴을 거쳐 10월 22일 발기인 대회를 개최했으며, 제로트러스트 보안협회는 KOTA 추진계획과 창립 초기 비용 지원을 승인했다. 기존 협회의 활동 기반을 수요자·공급자·전문가가 함께하는 구조로 넓혀 나가겠다는 것이다.

워킹그룹에서는 회원들이 공통으로 겪는 보안 과제를 선정하고 원인과 해결 방안을 연구한다. 결과는 기술 가이드, 참조모델, 보고서 등으로 정리할 계획이다. 공동 실증에서는 제안한 기술과 운영 방식이 실제 환경에서도 효과를 내는지 확인한다.

검증 범위에는 개별 제품의 기능뿐 아니라 서로 다른 보안기술의 연계 가능성, 운영상 문제, 도입 효과가 포함된다. 여러 기술과 접근통제 정책이 유기적으로 작동해야 하는 제로트러스트 환경에서 제품 사이의 단절을 줄이는 것이 중요한 과제다.

임종인 창립준비위원장인 김·장 법률사무소 고문은 인사말에서 AI를 활용한 위협 분석과 대응, 국내 보안제품 간 데이터 연계 필요성을 강조했다. 국내 기술을 연결해 한국형 보안 아키텍처를 구축하고, 이를 서비스 형태로 제공해 기업과 기관의 활용 범위를 넓히자는 구상도 제시했다.

실증 성과를 공유하는 과정에서 발생할 수 있는 이해관계도 운영 과제로 다뤘다. KOTA는 과제 착수 전에 참여기관의 역할과 인력·비용 분담, 결과 공개 범위, 지식재산권 등을 협의하도록 했다. 참여기관의 정보와 권리를 보호하면서 다른 기업도 활용할 수 있는 성과를 남기겠다는 방침이다.

창립선언문에는 기술 중립성과 공정한 참여, 실증과 증거에 따른 효과 판단, 정보·지식재산 보호, 투명한 재정 운영 등을 담은 10대 원칙을 명시했다.

2027년 중점 추진 방향으로는 산업별 특성을 반영한 제로트러스트 적용체계 고도화가 제시됐다.

김 회장은 같은 금융권이라도 대형 은행과 중소 금융회사의 환경이 다르다는 점을 지적했다. 공통적인 지침이 있어도 조직의 규모와 운영 조건을 반영한 보안 아키텍처가 필요하다는 것이다. KOTA는 수요기관의 구체적인 요구를 바탕으로 이러한 차이를 검토하고 적용 가능한 체계를 발전시킬 계획이다.

이는 공동 연구와 실증이 필요한 이유이기도 하다. 같은 기술을 도입해도 기존 시스템과 인력, 운영 방식에 따라 효과가 달라질 수 있는 만큼 실제 사용 조건에서 검증해야 한다는 취지다.

정부와의 협력 방향에 대해서는 먼저 민간 협력체로서 기반과 신뢰를 쌓겠다는 입장을 밝혔다. 연합 측은 특정 부처와의 관계를 우선하기보다 수요자가 과제를 제시하고 공급기업과 전문가가 해결·검증하는 구조를 먼저 정착시키겠다고 설명했다. 이를 토대로 정부 협력과 정책·제도 개선 과제를 구체화하겠다는 것이다.

초대 임원진에는 수요기관과 공급기업, 학계·법률 전문가들이 참여했다. 감사는 최동근 고려대학교 교수가 맡았으며, 임종인 김·장 법률사무소 고문과 김인석 법무법인 율촌 고문, 박춘식 전 아주대학교 교수가 자문에 참여한다.

KOTA가 내건 협력의 성패는 앞으로 공동 과제를 얼마나 구체적으로 선정하고, 검증 결과와 한계까지 공유하느냐에 달려 있다. 수요기관에는 도입과 운영의 시행착오를 줄이고, 공급기업에는 기술을 개선할 근거를 제공하는 실증 성과가 첫 시험대가 될 전망이다.

items.content:
인스피언이 모의해킹 및 보안컨설팅 전문기업 라온시큐리티의 지분 80%를 인수했다.

이번 인수는 기존 방어 중심의 기업 시스템 및 데이터 보호 기술에 공격자 관점의 취약점 진단 역량을 결합해 통합 보안 사업 영역을 넓히기 위한 결정이다.

2012년 설립된 라온시큐리티는 실제 해킹 기법을 활용한 모의해킹과 보안컨설팅을 주력으로 수행하는 기업이다. 금융기관, 통신사, 유통, 공공기관 등 여러 산업 분야에서 100건 이상의 보안 진단 프로젝트를 완료했다. 자체 개발한 모바일 앱 취약점 점검 솔루션 '자이로이드(Zyroid)'와 IoT 취약점 점검 도구 '시즈IoT(SiegeIoT)'를 보유하며 관련 기술력을 축적해 왔다.

인스피언은 자사의 SAP 보안, 개인정보 보호 등 기존 방어 보안 역량에 라온시큐리티의 공격 관점 보안 기술을 통합한다. 두 기업은 AI 기반 취약점 자동 진단과 공격 경로 분석, 상시 모의해킹 서비스(PTaaS)를 함께 개발한다. 단발성 점검을 넘어 지속적인 취약점 관리와 구독형 보안 서비스로 사업 구조를 확장할 계획이다.

양사는 인스피언이 기존 사업에서 확보한 600여 개 고객사와 라온시큐리티의 고객망을 활용해 교차판매를 진행하며 신규 매출 기회를 발굴한다. 인수 이후에도 라온시큐리티는 양정규 대표와 윤달형 최고기술책임자(CTO) 체제로 독립 운영된다. 인스피언은 향후 사업 성과에 따라 잔여 지분 20%를 단계적으로 추가 인수할 방침이다.

양정규 라온시큐리티 대표이사는 "인스피언의 고객 기반을 통해 기술 공급망을 넓히게 됐다"며 "자이로이드 고도화와 AI 기반 PTaaS 개발로 보안 진단 서비스 경쟁력을 높이겠다"고 말했다.

최정규 인스피언 대표이사는 "지능화되는 사이버 공격에 대응하려면 방어 기술과 함께 공격자의 관점에서 취약점을 먼저 찾아내는 역량이 중요해졌다"며, "양사의 기술을 결합해 기업 시스템을 선제적으로 보호하는 종합 보안기업으로 성장하겠다"고 밝혔다.

items.content:
오픈AI가 23일 서울 오픈AI 코리아 사무실에서 기업 서비스에 적용할 수 있는 보이스 모델과 API 주요 기능, 그리고 국내 기업 도입 사례를 발표했다.

이날 이재원 오픈AI 응용 AI 엔지니어는 실시간 대화와 다국어 소통에 특화된 모델들을 소개했다. 이용자와 실시간으로 대화하며 질문을 중간에 수정해도 곧바로 반영하는 ‘GPT-Live-1.1’, 음성을 같은 언어의 텍스트로 변환하는 ‘GPT-Live-Transcribe’, 실시간 통역을 제공하는 ‘GPT-Realtime-Translate’ 기능을 설명했다.

가상의 항공사 수하물 상담 데모에서는 승객이 대화 도중 목적지를 김포공항으로 변경하자, 기업 앱과 연동된 GPT-Live-1.1이 바뀐 요청을 즉각 반영해 수하물 정보를 다시 안내하는 과정을 시연했다.

이번 발표에서는 국내 스타트업 하이로컬이 오픈AI 보이스 기술을 산업 현장에 적용한 사례가 상세히 다뤄졌다. 하이로컬은 건설 및 제조 현장에서 한국어 소통에 어려움을 겪는 외국인 근로자를 돕기 위해 ‘하이워커’를 개발했다. 이 서비스는 오픈AI의 ‘gpt-4o-transcribe’와 실시간 소통을 지원하는 ‘Realtime API’ 등을 결합해 근로자가 안전 교육이나 작업 전 회의 내용을 모국어로 확인하고 질문할 수 있도록 지원한다. 근로자들은 별도의 앱 설치나 회원 가입 절차 없이 스마트폰으로 QR코드를 스캔해 서비스에 접속할 수 있다.

하이로컬은 다국어 소통 환경의 인식률을 높이기 위해 수년간 약 1000개 산업 현장에서 파악한 소음 데이터와 전문 공정 용어를 서비스에 직접 반영했다. 실제 국내 한 기업 실증 과정에서는 강사의 한국어 강의를 교육장 화면에 다국어 자막으로 띄우고, 교육생 각자의 스마트폰으로 번역 내용을 제공해 현장 교육 집중도를 크게 높였다.

한유하 오픈AI 스타트업 담당 디렉터는 "오픈AI의 기술이 산업 현장과 이용자를 깊이 이해하는 스타트업 서비스와 결합할 때 AI의 활용 범위가 더욱 넓어진다"며 "기술 적용 과정에서 스타트업의 현장 이해도가 매우 중요한 역할을 한다"고 말했다.

items.content:
이스트시큐리티가 앤트로픽의 사이버 검증 프로그램(CVP)에 합류했다. CVP는 앤트로픽이 검증된 보안 조직의 사이버 방어 업무를 지원하는 프로그램이다. 참여 기업은 허용된 업무 범위 내에서 사이버 보안 안전장치가 일부 조정된 AI 모델 클로드를 활용할 수 있다.

이스트시큐리티는 클로드를 이용해 자사가 소유하고 운영하는 소프트웨어와 시스템의 취약점을 찾아내고 파급력을 분석하는 내부 방어 연구를 진행한다. 오랜 기간 축적해 온 악성코드 분석 역량과 위협 인텔리전스에 클로드를 접목해, 새로운 취약점이 미치는 영향을 빠르게 파악하고 대응 우선순위를 결정할 방침이다.

연구 과정에서 확보한 데이터와 AI 활용 경험은 알약 에이전틱 EDR 등 자사 주요 보안 제품의 탐지 및 대응 기능 개선에 직접 반영한다. 최근 AI를 악용한 사이버 공격 기법이 정교해지고 동일한 취약점이 여러 국가와 산업에 동시다발적으로 영향을 미치는 환경에 대응하기 위한 조치다.

정상원 이스트시큐리티 대표는 "사이버 위협이 전 세계로 확산하고 있어 효과적인 방어를 위해서는 글로벌 공조가 필수적"이라며 "기존 엔드포인트 보안 기술을 바탕으로 국내외 기업 및 기관과 협력을 늘려 새로운 위협에 대한 대응 역량을 빠르게 끌어올리겠다"고 말했다.

이스트시큐리티는 앞서 공익 AI 보안 연합체인 프로젝트 캐노피에 방어 파트너로 참여한 데 이어 이번 CVP 합류를 결정하며 국내외 AI 보안 생태계 내 협력을 넓혀가고 있다.

items.title: Azure Flaw Exploited to Target Secrets at Norwegian Energy Firms
items.summary: Microsoft closed an Azure API Management flaw exploited to target secrets at Norwegian energy companies, with other sectors also affected. The post Azure Flaw Exploited to Target Secrets at Norwegian Energy Firms appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
A security issue discovered in Microsoft’s Azure API Management (APIM) service appears to have been responsible for the security incidents reported last week by two Norwegian energy firms, with impact extending beyond Norway.

Microsoft is notifying customers about the issue in Azure APIM, which is designed for publishing, securing and managing APIs. The vulnerability may have allowed threat actors to gain access to secrets stored in some APIM instances.

According to a private notification shared on Reddit by one customer, the tech giant discovered the issue on November 18 and closed the access path the next day.

“Our investigation found that customers were exposed and an unauthorized party could have used the issue to access secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before Microsoft identified the security issue,” Microsoft said.

Exposed data can include secrets stored as named values, client secrets for identity providers, subscription keys, and tokens for APIM’s direct management APIs.

Microsoft noted that APIM Classic tiers that don’t follow its documented security guidance are affected. Instances on v2 tiers are not impacted. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Norway’s National Security Authority (NSM) said on November 20 that the vulnerability had affected several organizations in the country, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi, which independently disclosed cybersecurity incidents last week.

Equinor reported the attack on November 17, one day before Microsoft identified the APIM flaw. The company said it found no evidence that data was stolen or altered. Skagerak Energi disclosed the incident on November 18, saying it did not impact operations or production, and it found no evidence of information compromise.

NSM said an unknown threat actor targeted tokens, secrets and named values stored in APIM. It’s unclear how widely the weakness has been exploited, but the organization noted that several sectors in Norway and abroad are impacted.

APIM users have been advised by NSM to treat their secrets and named values as compromised and replace them. They should also verify that their instances have been updated and identify the data accessible through the service.

Security expert Anders Kristiansen warned that credentials lifted from APIM could be used against outside services. The extent of the exposure depends on each credential’s permissions.

items.content:
인젠트의 개발자가 글로벌 오픈소스 데이터베이스인 PostgreSQL 19 버전 개발에 직접 참여해 총 9건의 코드 수정을 반영했다.

새롭게 출시된 19버전에는 서비스를 중단하지 않고 테이블을 정리하는 REPACK 명령과 서버 재시작 없이 활성화할 수 있는 논리 복제 등 운영 편의성을 높이는 신규 기능이 다수 포함됐다.

인젠트 AI연구본부 DB팀 소속 개발자는 올해 PostgreSQL 본 저장소에 총 10건의 커밋을 올렸다. 자신이 직접 작성한 수정 내역이 7건이며, 다른 개발자의 코드를 리뷰해 반영을 도운 건이 3건이다. 이 중 9건이 이번 19버전에 포함됐고 나머지 1건은 차기 버전에 적용된다. 직접 조치한 결함 중 4건은 이전 버전인 14부터 18버전까지 일괄 반영되면서 최근 배포된 정기 업데이트 및 19버전 릴리스 노트 기여자 명단에 이름을 올렸다.

해당 개발자는 현재 SQL 표준 기능 중 하나인 행 패턴 인식(RPR)을 공동 저자로 개발 중이다. RPR은 시간 순서대로 나열된 연속적인 데이터에서 특정 흐름을 찾아내는 기능이다. 주가 변동이나 거래 내역 등을 SQL만으로 정밀하게 분석할 수 있어 금융권 등에서 활용 가치가 높으며, 인젠트는 이를 향후 버전에 공식 반영하는 것을 목표로 삼고 있다.

이번 개발 참여는 인젠트가 오픈소스 DB를 단순히 채택해 쓰는 데 그치지 않고 코어 엔진 통제 역량을 갖췄음을 입증한다. 고객사 시스템에 문제가 발생했을 때 코드 단위에서 직접 원인을 분석하고 커뮤니티와 연계해 근본적인 해결책을 제시할 수 있다. 안정성이 필수적인 금융 및 공공기관이 오픈소스 기반 기술을 안심하고 도입할 수 있는 근거로 작용한다.

현재 인젠트는 PostgreSQL을 기반으로 고가용성, 백업 및 복구, 보안 등 엔터프라이즈 환경의 필수 기능을 패키지로 제공하는 통합 DBMS 플랫폼 eXperDB를 국내 주요 시장에 공급하고 있다.

이형배 인젠트 대표는 "오픈소스 데이터베이스를 단순히 쓰는 데 그치지 않고 직접 개선하는 데까지 참여하고 있다는 점에 의미가 있다"며 "이러한 역량을 바탕으로 금융·공공 고객이 안심하고 쓸 수 있는 데이터 플랫폼을 만들어 가겠다"고 말했다.

items.title: Norway says hackers exploited Microsoft security flaw to attack energy firms Equinor, Skagerak Energi
items.summary: Norwegian energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi were affected by a Microsoft cloud security vulnerability that hackers have exploited to target sensitive credentials, Norway's cybersecurity authorities said.
items.content:
The Mongstad refinery is Norway's largest and operated by Equinor. Credit: Ole Jørgen Bratland / Equinor Norway says hackers exploited Microsoft security flaw to attack energy firms Equinor, Skagerak Energi

Editor's note: This article was updated with comment from Microsoft at 1:00 p.m. EST on Monday.

Norwegian energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi are among the organizations affected by a Microsoft cloud security vulnerability that hackers have exploited to target sensitive credentials, Norway's cybersecurity authorities said.

The vulnerability affected Azure API Management (APIM), a Microsoft service that allows organizations to manage and secure connections between applications and other systems. According to Norway's National Security Authority (NSM), an unidentified threat actor has been actively targeting access tokens and other sensitive information stored in the platform.

Equinor, one of Europe's largest natural gas suppliers, and electricity producer Skagerak Energi both reported cyberattacks last week.

The vulnerability was first discovered by Norway's energy sector, with Equinor playing a key role in identifying the issue and alerting authorities, the agency said on Friday.

Equinor said it detected the attack last Tuesday but did not fully contain it until Friday. The incident disrupted some internal services, although the company's oil and gas production continued normally.

"There is no indication that data has been stolen or altered," Equinor said in its latest statement , adding that the attack did not appear to have specifically targeted the company.

Skagerak Energi, which produces and distributes electricity and is majority-owned by Norway's state-owned renewable energy company Statkraft, disclosed a separate cyberattack on Wednesday.

The company said the incident had not affected its operations or electricity production and that it had found no indication that information had been compromised.

In a non-public security advisory reportedly sent to customers and shared  by a purported recipient on Reddit, Microsoft said it discovered on November 18 a security issue affecting the older “Classic” tiers of Azure API Management and closed the access path the following day.

Microsoft warned that hackers may have accessed passwords and other sensitive information stored in vulnerable APIM systems before the company discovered the issue.

The problem mainly affected customers who had not followed Microsoft's security recommendations or had stored sensitive information directly in APIM instead of using Azure Key Vault, a separate service designed to keep such data secure. Newer versions of APIM were not affected, the company said.

Microsoft did not disclose how many customers may have been exposed or whether the same threat actor was responsible for the incidents involving the Norwegian energy companies.

On Saturday, Microsoft published guidance explaining how affected customers could identify and replace potentially exposed credentials. The guidance did not explicitly acknowledge the vulnerability or link it to the Norwegian attacks.

Microsoft told Recorded Future News it had identified and fixed a security flaw affecting several tiers of its Azure API Management service, including Developer, Basic, Standard and Premium. The company said it had notified potentially affected customers and provided guidance on how to protect their systems. A company spokesperson said they could not provide further details.

Norwegian authorities said the vulnerability affected organizations across multiple sectors in Norway and abroad.

"It remains unclear how extensively the vulnerability is being exploited or has been exploited in the past," said Martin Albert-Hoff, NSM's director of operational cybersecurity.

He added that authorities had found no evidence that successful or attempted compromises had disrupted services at Norwegian organizations.
